To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the real part of the complex dielectric permittyvity of soil samples of various salinity and particle size distributions depends on the volumetric water content of the soil, and the optimal frequency range for measuring soil moisture with the use of the real part of soil dielectric permittvity is between 150 and MHz.

the impact of soil particle-size distribution on the dielectric permittivities of the tested soils was negligible and the impact of soil salt content on the real part soil dielectric permittivites was significant and depended on the soil texture.

the real part of the dielectric permittivities of soils of different texture and salinity can differ up to 0.5, and the impact of salinity on the relation between soil moisture and real part of dielectrics permittivity can be minimized by the use of frequencies between 150 and1500 MHz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of salinity on the relation between soil moisture and dielectric permittivities in a wide frequency range.
the impact of salinity and texture on soil dielectric properties and it is focused on the frequency bands where the dielectric properties are the least affected by these two factors.
the impact of salinity on the dielectric permittivities of soils with different textures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the impact of soil particle-size distribution on the real part dielectric permittivities of soils of various salinities is significant, but the impact of soil texture is negligible for the soils with salinities below 1 dS/m.
the impact of salinity on the relation between soil moisture and dielectric permittivities is not significant for the soils of the examined particle-size distribution.
the impact of soil texture and salinity can be neglected in the frequency range of 150–500 MHz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of soil texture and salinity on the relation between soil moisture and dielectric permittivities is significant and it should be considered in soil moisture estimation.
the frequency bands of 150–500 MHz are the optimal ones for dielectric permittivities determination of saline soils.
the impact of soil texture on the dielectric properties of soils can be reduced by the use of the frequency bands between 150 and about 500 MHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of soil texture on the relation between soil moisture and dielectric permittivty is smaller than the impact of soil moisture.
soil salinity has a strong impact on the relation between soil volumetric water-content and the real part complex permittivity of soil.

the frequency band between 150 and about 500 MHz is the most appropriate for soil moisture determination by means of soil moisture-dielcetric permittivity calibration functions for soils with various salinity and texture.
